## World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO)

### What it does
The World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) is a specialized agency of the United Nations that promotes the protection of intellectual property worldwide. It provides global IP services including patent protection (via the PCT system), trademark registration (Madrid System), and industrial design rights (Hague System). WIPO also administers 26 international treaties related to intellectual property, engages in dispute resolution, supports technology transfer and innovation, and offers education and training in IP. Its mission is to lead the development of a balanced and effective international IP system that enables innovation and creativity for the benefit of all.

### Headquarters
WIPO is headquartered at **34, chemin des Colombettes, Geneva, Switzerland**. It has been based in Geneva since 1978. The majority of its staff positions are based at the Geneva headquarters, with additional offices in Tokyo and Singapore.

### Founding
WIPO was established by the WIPO Convention signed in Stockholm on **July 14, 1967**, and became a UN specialized agency in 1974. It currently has **194 member states**.

### Employees
Specific headcount figures are not available from the sources retrieved.

### Funding
WIPO describes itself as a **self-funding agency** of the United Nations — meaning it is largely financed through fees generated by its IP registration services (such as the PCT, Madrid, and Hague systems) rather than through UN assessed contributions. Its latest funding round is categorized as "Other Investors," with Hypergrowth Global listed as an investor.

### Latest funding round
The latest funding round on record is classified as **"Other Investors."**
